acceptance_criteria.criterion: GitResult, GitStatusInfo, BranchInfo, and CloneOptions types are exported from git.types.ts
runGit() spawns Git with shell: false and resolves with exit code, stdout, and stderr for both zero and non-zero exit codes
runGit() rejects the promise when the git binary is not found (ENOENT spawn error)
runGitOrThrow() returns trimmed stdout on success and throws on non-zero exit code
No shell injection is possible — shell: false is enforced and arguments are passed as an array

summary: Reviewed 2 files (src/git/git.types.ts, src/git/git-cli.ts). 0 Critical, 0 High, 2 Medium (noted), 0 Low. Security sign-off: PASS. Shell injection (A03) is fully mitigated — shell: false enforced and args passed as an array. Two medium findings documented for awareness: credential exposure via args in error messages, and unbounded output buffer growth.

comments.note: Medium | A02/A05 — Credential Exposure in Error Messages | src/git/git-cli.ts ~L64 | runGitOrThrow() constructs the error message via `args.join(' ')`. If a caller passes a git URL containing embedded credentials (e.g. https://user:pat@github.com/org/repo), those credentials will appear verbatim in the thrown Error.message and subsequently in any log, error-reporting service, or stack trace. Recommendation: redact credential-bearing URL segments before including args in error output, or limit the error message to the exit code and stderr only.

Medium | A04 — Unbounded Output Buffer Growth | src/git/git-cli.ts L32-33 | stdoutChunks and stderrChunks grow without bound. A git command producing very large output (e.g. git log --all on a large repository) can exhaust process heap memory. Recommendation: impose a per-stream byte cap and reject (or truncate with a warning) when the cap is exceeded.

summary: Code review PASS with one Fix-Forward applied. Both files (git.types.ts, git-cli.ts) are clean, well-architected, and correctly implement all 5 acceptance criteria. No Blocking issues found.

Fix-Forward applied: changed runGitOrThrow() error message from args.join(' ') to args[0] ?? '(unknown)' — this keeps the subcommand name (clone/log/fetch/etc.) while eliminating the credential-exposure risk the Security Auditor flagged for URLs embedded in args.

Architecture is solid: runGit() resolves for all exit codes (caller decides severity), rejects only on spawn failures, correctly uses Buffer.concat for cross-boundary UTF-8 safety. runGitOrThrow() is a clean thin wrapper with no surprises. shell: false enforced throughout.

comments.note: Applied Fix-Forward: src/git/git-cli.ts L64 — changed error message from `git ${args.join(' ')} failed` to `git ${args[0] ?? '(unknown)'} failed`. Eliminates credential exposure risk (credential-bearing URLs in args) raised by Security Auditor, while preserving the subcommand name for diagnostics. Non-behavioral change — no tests assert on this error message format.

[documentation-forward] git-cli.ts has no corresponding test file (src/tests/git-cli.test.ts). The public surface — runGit() resolve/reject contract, null exit code fallback, and runGitOrThrow() throw shape — should be documented in a test file or in the API docs so future contributors understand the expected behavior without reading the implementation.

Unbounded output buffer (stdoutChunks/stderrChunks) noted by Security Auditor is a future-phase concern. Acceptable for the current foundation WP, but a per-stream byte cap should be added before commands like `git log --all` are invoked on large repositories in later phases.
